title: Redemption
definition: Redemption is God's rescue of sinners from bondage and guilt through the price paid by Jesus Christ.
summary: Redemption is Christ's purchase of sinners out of bondage by the price of His blood.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the Redeemer who gives Himself as the ransom for sinners and liberates them for God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Redemption means Christ frees His people by paying the price of their deliverance. Scripture uses the language of ransom, slavery, blood, and release to show the cost of salvation.

Believers are not redeemed with silver, gold, or self-effort. They are bought by the precious blood of Christ and therefore no longer belong to the old masters of sin, fear, and condemnation.

Jesus is the Redeemer who gives His life as a ransom. Redemption shows that freedom is costly, personal, and secured by the Savior's sacrifice.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people want freedom without understanding the price paid to obtain it. This doctrine keeps freedom connected to the blood of Christ and protects believers from returning to slavery.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Live as someone bought by Christ. Do not give yourself back to masters He redeemed you from, and let gratitude for His costly ransom shape worship, holiness, and compassion for those still enslaved.
